title: API Reference
content:
#


⚠️ Important Version Notes#


v0.0.5 (current)#

A patch release that fixes missing useStorage exports in subpath entries, writes
during render in getSnapshot, and adds manager recycling APIs. See the
changelog.


v0.0.4 breaking changes#

 1. Vue immediate now defaults to false: the value is initialized from storage
    instead of being written back on creation. Pass immediate: true when you
    need the initial value persisted immediately.
 2. ParseStrType.EVAL is deprecated: it uses new Function and throws under
    strict CSP (e.g. hardened Tauri or Electron). Use JSON or AUTO instead.
 3. UMD output extension changed to .cjs: importing through the package name or
    subpaths is unaffected.


Migration guide#

Old versions (v0.0.1-beta.8 and earlier):



v0.0.3+: import from the framework-specific subpath.



Legacy names such as useReactStorage are still exported as aliases but are no
longer recommended.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Shared Options#

All frameworks share BaseStoreOptions<T>:

PROPERTY         TYPE                                           DEFAULT                              DESCRIPTION
storage          StoreType                                      StoreType.LOCAL                      Storage area: LOCAL or SESSION
parse            'json' | 'auto'                                'json'                               Deserialization mode
serializer       (value: T) => string | null | undefined        -                                    Custom serializer; returning null / undefined rejects the
                                                                                                     write
deserializer     (raw: string) => T                             -                                    Custom deserializer
version          number                                         -                                    Data version used together with migrate
migrate          (oldValue: unknown, oldVersion: number) => T   -                                    Migrates old data on read and writes the result back
equals           (a: T, b: T) => boolean                        Reference / JSON string comparison   Skips writes and notifications when equal
memoryFallback   boolean                                        true                                 Falls back to memory when storage is unavailable or a write
                                                                                                     fails
onError          (ctx: StorageErrorContext) => void             -                                    Error callback; ctx contains key, storage, operation, and
                                                                                                     error

> The same key + storage area shares one manager. options and initialValue only
> take effect on first creation.


Parse modes#

 * json (default): strict JSON; parsing failures fall back to the initial value.
 * auto: compatible with legacy bare strings. On read, only strings starting
   with {, [, or " are parsed as JSON; everything else is returned as-is. On
   write, strings are stored as-is and other types still use JSON.stringify.

With auto, numbers and booleans are written as JSON and may come back as
strings; use json when strict types matter.


StorageActions#

The third return value in React, Preact, and Solid, and the returned object in
Svelte and Vanilla expose:

MEMBER     DESCRIPTION
key        The current storage key
remove()   Removes the key and falls back to the initial value
clear()    Clears only keys managed by this library; it never calls
           native storage.clear()
manager    The underlying manager instance


Low-level manager API#



API                                              DESCRIPTION
getStorageManager(key, initialValue, options?)   Gets or creates the shared manager for a key
retainStorageManager(key, storage?)              Acquires a reference; pair it with releaseStorageManager
releaseStorageManager(key, storage?)             Releases a reference; recycles in a microtask when the count
                                                 reaches zero and there are no subscribers
getRegisteredManagers(storage?)                  Returns registered managers
clearManagedStorage(storage?)                    Removes all keys managed by this library
clearStorageManagerRegistry()                    Destroys and removes every manager (for tests / HMR)

Framework adapters automatically retain and release on mount and unmount. Manual
instances and non-component scenarios must do it themselves. When using Vue
outside setup, wrap the call in effectScope() and release with scope.stop().

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Framework Adapters#


useStorage (Vue)#

Signature#



Options#

In addition to the shared options, Vue supports:

PROPERTY    TYPE      DEFAULT   DESCRIPTION
immediate   boolean   false     Writes the current value back to storage on creation
deep        boolean   true      Watches nested mutations

Other Vue watch options are also supported.

Return value#

A Ref<T> kept in sync with the selected storage area.

Example#




useStorage (React)#

Signature#



Built on useSyncExternalStore, with React 18+ concurrent rendering and SSR
support (getInitialSnapshot() returns the initial value on the server).

Return value#

 * [0]: the current value T
 * [1]: updater supporting setValue(next) and setValue(prev => next)
 * [2]: { key, remove, clear, manager }

Example#




useStorage (Preact)#

Same three-element tuple as React:




useStorage (Solid)#

Returns [Accessor<T>, setter, StorageActions<T>]:




useStorage (Svelte)#

Returns a Svelte store with set / update / remove / clear / destroy:




useStorage (Angular)#

Call it inside an injection context (component or service). Return value:





The manager is released when the component's DestroyRef fires.


useStorage (Vanilla JS)#

Both the root entry and /vanilla resolve to the vanilla adapter:



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Utilities#


parseStr#



PARAMETER   TYPE           DEFAULT             DESCRIPTION
str         string         -                   String to parse
type        ParseStrType   ParseStrType.JSON   JSON, AUTO, or the deprecated EVAL



> ParseStrType.EVAL is deprecated and throws under strict CSP. Do not use it in
> new code.


isValidJSON#




isStorageEnabled#



Checks whether storage is usable (Safari private mode, quota limits, etc.). The
result is cached.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Enums#


StoreType#




ParseStrType#



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Legacy API#

Before v0.0.1-beta.8, useStorage defaulted to immediate: true and React used a
separate useReactStorage. Those interfaces are kept for compatibility only and
behave differently:

 * Vue's old useStorage default for immediate is now false.
 * useReactStorage is now an alias of useStorage, whose return value is a
   three-element tuple.
 * The old parseStr only supported JSON / EVAL; AUTO was added and EVAL is
   deprecated.

New projects should use the unified APIs above.

title: Changelog
content:
#

All notable changes to this project are documented on this page. This project
adheres to Semantic Versioning.


[0.0.5] - 2026-11-16#

A patch release focused on subpath exports and lifecycle cleanup.


Fixed#

 * Missing useStorage in subpath entries: the React, Vue, Preact, Solid, Svelte,
   and Angular entries only exported useXxxStorage, so the documented ``
   returned undefined. Both names are now available, and the old aliases still
   work.
 * getSnapshot wrote to storage during render: version migration used to write
   back inside getSnapshot, violating the purity requirement of
   useSyncExternalStore. Migration results are now persisted on non-render paths
   such as subscribe, external changes, and setValue.
 * console.error was still emitted when onError was configured: now only the
   callback runs.
 * Added "./package.json" to exports for tooling that reads the package
   manifest.


Added#

 * Manager recycling: retainStorageManager / releaseStorageManager. The registry
   decides whether to recycle based on the reference count and subscriber count,
   and defers removal to a microtask so React StrictMode's mount → unmount →
   remount does not drop an instance that is still in use.
 * Automatic release in adapters: all 7 framework adapters release the manager
   on unmount. In Angular, even when StorageService is providedIn: 'root', the
   caller component's DestroyRef is used; in Svelte, a recycled instance is
   re-acquired automatically on the next subscription.


Docs#

 * Corrected the bundle size claim from "under 1 KB" to about 4 KB gzipped.
 * Documented the React 18+ requirement, dedupe for duplicate installs, dynamic
   key cleanup, and a complete effectScope example for Vue usage outside setup.
 * Fixed Chinese navigation and in-page links.


Known Limitations#

 * With parse: 'auto', numbers and booleans are still written as JSON and may
   come back as strings; use the default json mode when strict types matter.


[0.0.4] - 2026-11-16#

A refactoring release focused on stability, predictability, and packaging.


Breaking Changes#

 * Vue immediate now defaults to false: the value is initialized from storage
   without an extra write on creation. Pass immediate: true explicitly if you
   want the initial value persisted immediately.
 * ParseStrType.EVAL is deprecated: it relies on new Function, which throws
   under strict CSP (e.g. hardened Tauri / Electron). Use JSON or the new AUTO
   instead.
 * UMD artifacts now use the .cjs extension: main and every exports.require
   entry have been updated. Importing by package name or subpath is unaffected;
   only direct references to the old UMD filenames need updating.


Added#

 * Shared instance per key: every component using the same key and storage area
   shares one manager within a tab, so setValue syncs immediately.
 * Functional updates: setValue(prev => next), matching the React useState
   updater pattern.
 * parse mode: 'json' (default, strict JSON) and 'auto' (keeps legacy raw
   strings such as 'dark' and '1' readable).
 * remove() / clear(): remove() deletes the current key and falls back to the
   initial value; clear() removes only keys owned by this library.
 * Versioned migration: version + migrate(oldValue, oldVersion) upgrades stored
   data on read and writes it back.
 * Custom serialization: serializer / deserializer for Date, Map, Set, etc.
   Returning null / undefined from serializer skips the write.
 * Equality check: equals(a, b) defaults to reference or JSON string comparison
   and skips writes and notifications when values are equal.
 * Storage fallback and error hook: memoryFallback (default true) switches to
   in-memory storage when storage is unavailable or a write fails; onError({
   key, storage, operation, error }) makes logging and reporting easy.
 * Richer adapter return values: React / Preact / Solid return [value, setValue,
   { key, remove, clear, manager }]; the Svelte store adds remove / clear /
   destroy; Angular and Vanilla expose setValue / updateValue / reset / remove /
   clear.
 * SSR support: the React adapter now uses useSyncExternalStore, and
   getInitialSnapshot() returns the initial value during server rendering.
 * Core exports: StorageManager, getStorageManager, getRegisteredManagers,
   clearManagedStorage, clearStorageManagerRegistry, and related types.


Fixed#

 * Multiple components using the same key in one tab no longer drift out of
   sync.
 * Storage quota errors and setItem failures in Safari private mode no longer
   break state updates.
 * Vue deep-watch in-place mutations (same reference) are now persisted.
 * Accessing window during SSR no longer throws.
 * Removing a key now also cleans up its version marker.
 * Cross-tab storage events now handle clear() and version marker changes
   correctly.


Tooling and Packaging#

 * Added a files whitelist so only dist and the READMEs are published.
 * sideEffects: false; types is listed first in exports for better tree-shaking
   and type resolution.
 * peerDependencies.react is now >=18.0.0, the self-dependency was removed, and
   the package has zero runtime dependencies.
 * Expanded the behavior-level test matrix to cover same-tab multiple instances,
   cross-tab sync, SSR, key switching, functional updates, raw strings, quota
   errors, clear, and version migration.


[0.0.3] - 2025-09-15#


Added#

 * Multi-framework support: adapters for React, Preact, Solid, Svelte, Angular,
   and Vanilla JavaScript.
 * Framework-specific entry points: ew-responsive-store/react, /vue, /preact,
   /solid, /svelte, /angular, and /vanilla.
 * Unified API: every framework exposes the same useStorage function name.


Changed#

 * Framework dependencies moved to peerDependencies and are externalized from
   the bundle to keep the package small.
 * useReactStorage from the legacy entry is replaced by useStorage imported from
   the React entry.


[0.0.2] - 2025-02-17#


Changed#

 * Dependency and build configuration updates; stabilizes the 0.0.1 line.


[0.0.1] - 2024-12-24#


Added#

 * First stable release: useStorage built on Vue's reactivity system, making
   localStorage / sessionStorage data reactive.
 * Supports primitives, objects, and arrays, with storage, deep, and immediate
   options.
 * Ships parseStr, isValidJSON, isStorageEnabled, and complete TypeScript types.

> Earlier 0.0.1-beta.0 through 0.0.1-beta.9 were pre-release iterations that
> mainly introduced the React useReactStorage hook, cross-tab synchronization,
> and type definitions, and are not listed individually.

title: Getting Started
content:
#


Introduction#

If your project requires using web storage (either localStorage or
sessionStorage) to persist data, and you want the data to be retained after a
page refresh while also automatically updating the view when the data changes,
ew-responsive-store is the perfect solution.

It's about 4 KB gzipped and extremely easy to use. With just a single function
call, you can make storage data reactive, which can be applied to any
framework-based project, even native JavaScript projects. The library also
includes comprehensive unit tests and type inference.


Installation#

First, you need to install the ew-responsive-store package. You can install it
using the following command:




Framework Dependencies#

Since v0.0.3, ew-responsive-store supports multiple frameworks. You only need to
install the framework you're using:



Note: Framework dependencies are treated as external, so they won't be bundled
with your application, keeping the library size minimal.


Environment and Dependency Notes#

 * React 18+: The React adapter is built on useSyncExternalStore, and
   peerDependencies requires react >= 18. React 17 and earlier are not
   supported.
 * Avoid duplicate installs: Same-tab sync relies on a module-level registry. If
   multiple copies of ew-responsive-store are installed (multiple versions, a
   monorepo without hoisting, or a package manager that did not dedupe), the
   registry is split and components sharing the same key will not sync. Run npm
   dedupe / pnpm dedupe / yarn dedupe, or configure resolve.dedupe:
   ['ew-responsive-store'] in Vite.
 * Dynamic key cleanup: Framework adapters release the manager automatically on
   unmount. For manually created instances or non-component scenarios, call
   releaseStorageManager(key, storage); the instance is removed from the
   registry and destroyed in a microtask. When using Vue outside setup, wrap the
   call in effectScope() and call scope.stop() to release automatically. In
   Angular, call it within an injection context (component/service), otherwise
   release manually.


Framework-Specific Imports#

Since v0.0.3, you should import from framework-specific entry points:




Basic Usage#

The root entry of ew-responsive-store exports the vanilla JavaScript useStorage,
along with StoreType, ParseStrType, the StorageManager APIs, and utilities such
as parseStr, isValidJSON, and isStorageEnabled. The root useStorage turns
localStorage / sessionStorage data into a reactive object; for Vue, React, and
other frameworks, use their dedicated subpath entries.


Basic Values#

You can use useStorage to create reactive basic values. For example, let's say
you have a counter stored in localStorage:



Vue Template Code:



At this point, the value of count is stored in the browser's session storage,
and it is reactive, meaning it will persist even after the page refreshes and
the view will update automatically when the value changes.


Object Values#

You can also store reactive objects in a similar way:



When you change the name property of userInfo, the view will automatically
update, and the data will be saved in session storage.


Array Values#

You can also store arrays, and they will be reactive as well:




Using Outside setup (effectScope)#

The Vue adapter releases the storage manager on unmount via onScopeDispose. When
you call it outside setup or an effectScope (e.g. a module-level singleton,
Pinia store initialization, or a utility function), there is no lifecycle to
hook into, so create an explicit scope:



Notes:

 * scope.stop() also stops watchers and reactive effects inside the scope;
   afterwards settings is no longer synced with storage.
 * If effectScope is not an option, release manually. The key and storage area
   must match the ones used at creation:



 * Calling useStorage directly inside a component's setup needs no extra
   handling; unmount releases it automatically.

For more advanced usage and configuration options, check out the API Reference
section.
